translation:
Then Vaishnav Jivandasji said, "This gathering-place belongs to Namdev and Kabir. If there is any feeling of ownership here, the soul will not attain the Supreme Lord -- this place is only for coming together to sing Govind's glories."

_Sabke sadguru Kabirji, mamat karo jin koi. Aur duniyaku Jivana, sadguru dharki joi. ||8||_ (Kabirji is the true guru of all -- let none hold obstinate pride or rivalry over this. As for the rest of the world, O Jivan, it is the wife of the household who serves as their guru.)

[Najar Samagam p.165; Manuscript 98, p.37; Manuscript 79, p.37] Maharaj Jivandasji says: Kabirji is the world-guru (jagadguru) of the entire universe, so regarding this hold no stubborn insistence, no urge to win, and enter into no dispute. But for all people besides those who practise loving devotion (prem-bhakti), the worldly, illusion-bound wife of their household is their guru.

Trikamdas Gordhandas wrote Kundli-3 on page 1 of his diary of Samvat 2032:

_Sabke sadguru Kabirji, mamat karo jin koi. Aur duniyaku Jivana, sadguru dharki joi. Sadguru dharki joy, maya chhe mahaduhkh deti. Nugra na raheso koy, samaj vin nishphal kheti. Trikam anubhav soy, kahe chhe Shri Guru Jivanji. Mamat karo jin koy, sabke sadguru Kabiraji._ (Kabirji is the true guru of all -- let none hold rivalry over this. For the rest of the world, O Jivan, the household wife is their guru, and as household-guru she gives them great sorrow through maya. Never remain without a guru, for effort made without understanding turns out fruitless. This is Trikam's own realized experience, so says the revered Guru Jivanji: hold no rivalry over this -- Kabirji is the true guru of all.)

Kabirji is the true guru of the entire world, so hold no stubbornness or dispute on this matter. But for everyone except those who practise loving devotion, it is their own household wife who is their guru -- and as household guru, this worldly illusion causes them great suffering. So never remain without any guru at all, because any effort made without understanding turns out fruitless. Trikam says that Sadguru Jivanji has spoken this from his own experience, so hold no obstinate doubt or suspicion about the fact that Kabirji is the guru of all.

_Swamise Hari sath kos, kirtaniya se bis. Harijanke hirde basai, sevakjanke sees. ||9||_ (From a mere renunciant, Hari stays sixty kos away; from a mere kirtan-singer, twenty kos away. He dwells in the heart of the true devotee, and upon the head of the true servant.)

In the section on hypocrisy (Kapat-ka-Ang), Das Kabirji says: from a mere shaven-headed renunciant, God stays sixty kos away; from one who does only kirtan-singing, He stays twenty kos away. He dwells in the heart of the true devotee (one who yearns for Him in separation), and He resides in the head -- the very life-breath -- of the servant-devotee.

_Grihike hirdai basau, vairagike sees._ (He dwells in the heart of the householder, and upon the head of the renunciant.)

[Nani, Notebook No. 2, p.75] He dwells in the hearts of householders and upon the heads of renunciants.

(The Proclamation of Baba Kabirji)

_Kabir swami ko nahi, swami sarajanhar. Swami hokar baith hi, te dhano sahego mar. ||10||_ (Says Kabir: there is no other master in this world; the Creator alone is the Master. Whoever sits enthroned claiming mastership will have to bear much suffering.)

This is the proclamation of Baba Das Kabir. Das Kabirji says: in this world there is no owner or master at all besides God, the Creator of the universe. But whoever lays claim to mastership will have to endure great suffering.

Trikamdas Gordhandas writes a Kundli on page 141 of his diary of Samvat 2030:

_Kabir swami ko nahi, swami sarajanhar, swami hokar baith hi, te dhano sahego mar, bahot sahego mar, sadguru kahai pokari, mudhan samje lagar, akkal gai jeni mari, kahe Trikam thoki nagar, sathno sang chhodi sahi, swami sarajan har, Kabir swami ko nahi._ (Says Kabir: there is no master in this world, the Creator alone is the Master. Whoever sits enthroned as master will have to bear great suffering -- very great suffering, so the sadguru cries out and proclaims. Fools do not understand this in the least, for their wits have deserted them. Beating the drum, Trikam says: truly give up the company of the wicked -- the Creator alone is the Master; says Kabir, there is no other master.)

Das Kabirji says: no one in this world can truly hold the position of master; only God, the Creator of the universe, is the Master of the world. But if anyone claims the right of mastership, he will have to bear great suffering from the bonds of karma. Sadguru Kabir cries out emphatically that such people will have to suffer greatly. Yet fools do not understand even this much, for their good sense has completely deserted them. Beating the drum, Trikam says it is best to give up the company of the wicked, because the only Master is God, the Creator of the universe -- there is no other master besides Him.

(The Couplet Describing the Realm of the Vaishnavs)

_Kabir swami sevak jahan nahi, jahan nahi jap aur jaap. Gun avgunki gam nahi, jahan nahi punya aur paap. ||11||_ (Says Kabir: there, there is no master and no servant, no chanting and no japa; there is no concern for virtue or vice, no sin and no merit.)

This describes the abode in which the Vaishnavs -- the devotees -- dwell. Das Kabirji says that there, no one is anyone's master and no one is anyone's servant, and no one need chant or repeat anyone's name. There, good and bad qualities have no effect at all, and there is no such thing as sin or merit either.

The Master there has no sense of being a master, and among the servants there is no sense of being a servant -- this itself is the mark of a true Vaishnav.

_Rup rekh kachhu vapu nahi, aise Raghupatiray. Aise harijan Jivana, naam nirmal jas gaay. ||12||_ (Raghupati -- Ram -- has no form, shape, or bodily mark at all, such is He; and such, O Jivan, is the true devotee too, who sings the pure, spotless glory of His Name.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: just as Raja Ram has no form, shape, or bodily figure of any kind, in the very same way God's devotees, too, are without form or feature -- they who worship the pure, holy Name of God.

Revered Yadunath writes in Litiyu (notebook) No. 46, page 18: "formless" means without any shape at all, for whatever has shape also carries the three gunas (qualities of nature). This is a matter worth studying through the Gita; in this Samagam, Jivanji has drawn upon the Gita.

Vaishnav Jivandasji said, "The festivals of Gokul Ashtami and Ram Navami belong to the Merciful Lord (Kripanath). Do not wait for a large group to gather -- whatever each of you can manage to bring, bring that. Keep this instruction of mine: come together and sing the glories of Govind."

(The Sakhi Spoken by His Own Holy Mouth)

_Aap aapni taapani, taapat hai sab koi. Milkar taape Jivana, je sadguruka hoi. ||13||_ (Everyone warms himself at his own fire alone; but, O Jivan, those who truly belong to the sadguru warm themselves together, side by side.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says that everyone, following their own private inclination, undertakes bhajan and devotion on their own terms, wilfully undergoing hardship through japa, austerity, and similar practices by themselves. But those who practise devotion under the sadguru's instruction join together with one another and perform bhajan-kirtan and the like in a way that gives everyone warmth and support.

Maharaj Adhyaruji has said in the Ghodli kirtan:

_Ghodli ja ghat rup anant, guru vachne sahu ek hoe. ||Gho.15||_ (O Ghodli, in every body dwells the Infinite; through the guru's word, all become one.)

O devotee mounted upon the steed of divine love! Just as many different opinions appear among all embodied beings, yet when all of them come under the guru's instruction, they become of one mind. Such a devotee, mounted on the steed of divine love, attains the Lord's refuge.

Vaishnav Jivandasji said, "Have my seat made beneath the lemon tree." He had all the women called. He said to the women, "Bring water for bathing, so that I may wash away my mastership [my worldly identity as 'Swami']." (That is, he told the women to bring the water heated.)

Revered Yadunath writes in Litiyu No. 21, page 37, regarding the title "Swami": Vadhji (of Gordhan Sargai) had once asked Madhavlal, the Swami of the Hansapura seat, "We are the swami [husband] of your wife -- so master of what are you?" -- and was told that the title "Swami" is used with reference to Padmanabh Swami. He was told to ask Trikam about the surname "Swami" in the court case (in the Trust case).

Revered Yadunath told me (Jagdish) that we are followers of Padmanabh Swami, and that is why our surname is "Swami." He also told me that while other people are swami (master) of a wife, we, however, are swami of Indi.

He said to all the women, "Place tulsi leaves upon my head." The women placed tulsi leaves upon him. Then Jivandasji said, "That is enough." He called out to Somdasji and said, "Take my body to the garden at Shahpura and perform the cremation there. There, make a Ram-shila (a tulsi platform). Carry me to that garden." Having said this, Somdasji replied, "Your word shall be obeyed."

_Taham Ajodhya jaham Raghupati, kahannad tam Gokul gaam. Satapuri taham Jivana, jaham sant sangat Hari naam. ||14||_ (Wherever Raghupati is, there is Ayodhya; wherever Krishna is, there is the village of Gokul. But, O Jivan, wherever there is the company of saints and the Name of Hari, there all the seven sacred cities dwell together.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: wherever Ram is present, only Ayodhyapuri alone is there; and wherever Krishna is present, only Mathurapuri alone is there. But wherever there is the company of saints together with the Name of Hari, there all seven of the sacred cities are present at once.

And he said, "Keep the garden at Puniyad reserved." He then also said, "You will not be able to manage carrying me all the way from Puniyad to Shahpura for the cremation while singing kirtan, nor will you be able to perform any other rite or exertion on my behalf after I am gone. But do dress me in clean, white garments. As much as you are able, sing kirtan and recite katha, and then return home." And he said, "Women, bring the thali, so that we may offer it to the Merciful Lord." Everyone went to fetch the thali. They brought the plate of offerings and placed it at his feet. Vaishnav Jivandasji then offered it to the Merciful Lord, and said, "Let this prasad reach every village where there is tilak and tulsi, wherever my beloved ones are." The prasad was given to all the Vaishnavs, and all those present received the great prasad.

This meant that they would not be able to carry him all the way from Puniyad to Shahpura for the cremation while singing kirtan, nor would they be able to perform any rite or undergo any hardship on his behalf after his passing -- but they were to dress him in clean garments.

At this word, they experienced great joy. Then he said, "The garden at Shahpura belongs to Mota Gopalji. Before the present gathering of Vaishnavs came into being, I had come to Mota Gopal's temple."

In Rest (Vishram) 1, verses 5 and 7, of Maharaj Jivanji's Parcharji (hagiography), there is mention that Mota Gopaldasji gave shelter at Shahpura to Jivandasji when he was wandering at the age of eleven.

_Gaanv Shahapuro taham kahave, sant mandali Harigun gaave. -5_ (There a village called Shahapuro was known; there a company of saints sang the glories of Hari.)

_Sant ek milyo taham aavi, hamare grihmein rahenge bhai. -7_ (One saint came there and met him, saying, "Brother, come and stay in my house.")

There was a village named Shahpura where a company of saints used to sing the praises of Hari. There, a saint -- Mota Gopaldas -- came and met him. He said to him (to Jivanji), "Come and stay in my house."

Then the Merciful Lord's (Jivanji's) order came to be that the cremation should take place at Mota Gopal's garden. Out of quiet regard for Gopaldasji, who had given him shelter in Samvat 1660, he had at first remained silent about this, and so asked for the cremation to be at Shahpura instead of Puniyad. But when Shyamdasji recited Jivanji's fourteenth sakhi, he then said that the cremation should be given at the garden of Puniyad.

He confirmed the tulsi garden of Puniyad as the chosen garden, saying, "Make a Ram-shila there." At that time, invitations for the festival were sent out. Then, as everyone gathered there, all the Vaishnavs together prepared the provisions and cooked dishes. Then, having taken his seat beneath the lemon tree, he asked Samdasji for water to bathe. Samdasji brought water and placed it before Vaishnavji. Then Jetibai, Malibai, Panabai, and other women brought the thali of prasad.

The kirtan continued unceasingly. At midnight, Lachhbai came from Thonhavi, and together with her, Ramabai and Tulsidas also came. Meeting these Vaishnavs amid the gathered Vaishnavs, Vaishnavji felt very great joy.

On the second day, the Vaishnavs of Bhilupur arrived. When it was the last watch of the night, the Vaishnav Mohandas brought a plate of kamod-rice from Hansapura. He had that plate of kamod-rice prasad brought forward. Jivandasji partook of that prasad, and all those present in the gathering received that great prasad.

Then Kahandas asked, "Vaishnavji, what do you have to say?" Vaishnavji then spoke: "In the Vraja clan, the Vedas summoned Brahma; the Vedas sang of that being of light. In the Vraja clan, the Vedas summoned Brahma to that being of light -- He, the charming flute-player, is the true Supreme Lord." This episode concerning Brahma he thus related.

After that, Harmabai showed great heartfelt concern and care for him, and she received Vaishnavji's grace. Vaishnavji then said further, "However much one instructs and admonishes the soul (jiva) in many ways, the soul does not give up its own ignorance (avidya). That ignorance is given up only if one becomes a true guru-oriented soul (gurumukhi) -- then the ignorance is given up. But the soul is not guru-oriented -- so what happens then? For this very reason it is said: the tilak and tulsi are the sign of Kabirji, the sign of the Great One. Whoever bears the tilak and tulsi is called a gurumukh (one turned toward the guru). Otherwise, no one truly becomes a gurumukh."

(The Sakhi about this)

_Dasatan sab manmate, gurumate ko naahi. Gurumate te Jivana, je Haricharan kamalki chhanhi. ||15||_ (All service as practised is done by one's own mind's inclination; hardly any is done by the guru's instruction. But, O Jivan, that which follows the guru's instruction alone reaches the shade of Hari's lotus feet.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: whoever, having become a surrendered devotee of God's guru, nevertheless practises devotion according to his own private will and does not accept the guru's instruction, cannot be called a gurumukh. But if he practises devotion by following the guru's instruction, he attains refuge in God's own abode.

Trikamdas Gordhandas wrote Kundli 22 on page 116 of his diary of Samvat 2025:

_Dasatan sab man mato, gurumato koi nahi, gurumato te Jivana, je Haricharan kamalki chhanhi, Haricharan kamalki chhanhi, phari nahi garbhma aave, gurugam vin jag manhi, kadi nahi shanti paave, manmate na malse Sai, duhkhi thai jaso din jate, gurumato koi nahi, dasatan sab man mato._ (All service is done by one's own mind's inclination; hardly any is done by the guru's instruction. That which is done by the guru's instruction, O Jivan, reaches the shade of Hari's lotus feet -- and once in that shade, one never enters the womb again. Without the guru's guidance, one never finds peace anywhere in this world. Following one's own mind, one will not find the Lord, and as the days pass one will only grow more sorrowful. Hardly any devotion is done by the guru's instruction -- all service is done by one's own mind's inclination.)

Those who have set themselves up as devotees of God according to their own private will do not follow the guru's instruction. But if one practises devotion following the guru's instruction instead, one reaches the lotus feet of God. Once having reached God's lotus feet, one does not enter the womb again. Without obtaining the secret of devotion from the guru, one can never attain peace and will, in the end, become sorrowful -- because such a person does not practise devotion according to the guru's instruction, but everyone instead practises devotion according to their own will.

Whoever, by the guru's instruction, has taken up the tilak and tulsi -- such a great soul's faults, Vasudevji (God) does not hold in His heart. So who, then, could ever call such a person guru-less? He is called "great" precisely because Vasudevji does not hold that person's faults against him in His heart.

Having spoken on this matter, Vaishnavji said to Harmaba, "Stay here until my festival [death-anniversary celebration]. After the festival is complete, come again on the fifth." A time was fixed; Harmabai made this request to Vaishnavji. Then, when there remained one ghadi (about twenty-four minutes) of the day left, Kahandas asked him -- on that fifth day he asked, "Vaishnavji, what do you have to say?" He then replied, "Brother, in Vrindavan...

...the Vedas summoned Brahma there, and that being of light is truly Shri Krishna. Whoever the Vedas and Brahma speak of, that being of light of which the Vedas spoke -- as proof of that, Shri Krishna revealed Himself to Brahma. That being of light was Shri Krishna, who in the Vraja clan comes as the Merciful Lord grazing cattle. At that very time Brahma performed the arati of Shri Krishna -- that is when it happened. All the Vaishnavs who have come here are singing the glory of Govindji."

Kahandasji asked, "What do you have to say?" Just then Haribhai arrived from Aridha, along with all the other Vaishnavs. Haribhai bowed to Vaishnavji. Accepting Haribhai's bow, Vaishnavji looked upon all the Vaishnavs and addressed the entire assembly as "Ram-Kabir." He said, "Sing the song of Vighna-haran [remover of obstacles]." The Vaishnavs sang five verses -- and as they sang, Vaishnav Jivandasji departed for his own divine abode (swadham), while the kirtan to Hari surged on in waves.

Revered Yadunath writes in Litiyu No. 6, page 62: "If a train is scheduled to leave the station at ten o'clock, then it leaves at ten -- no one asks why it left at ten and not a quarter past ten." In the same way, Maharaj Jivanji's time to depart came exactly as the fifth verse was being sung. As soon as the five verses were sung, Maharaj departed.

There Kahandasji spoke this couplet:

_Baiyan biji vaar, nahi aave aiso davdo. Maya malse kaimvaar, pan nahi hoy sant melawdo. ||16||_ (O sisters, such an occasion will never come a second time. Worldly wealth may be found again and again, but a gathering of saints such as this will never occur again.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: O devotees of the gopi-bhava (the feminine devotional mood toward the Lord), who have set aside effort through japa, austerity, pilgrimage, vows, mantra, and spiritual practice in favour of that mood of devotion -- the opportunity of this human birth, and of this company of saints that you now have, will not come again and again. Worldly wealth (maya) may indeed be gained many times over, but the good fortune of being together with the saints will not be found again. So gather together with the saints now and complete your devotion to God. This moment will not come again and again.

_Samvat sattarsen saatatris, sud panchami Bhadur maas. Ta din Jivandasji, liyo swadham nivaas. ||17||_ (In the year Samvat 1737, on the fifth of the bright half of the month of Bhadrapad, on that day Jivandasji took up residence in his own divine abode.)

On the fifth day of the bright half of Bhadrapad in Samvat 1737, Jivandasji departed for his own divine abode. Note: this account was completed, as received in a dream at Bhilpur, on the second day of the bright half of Magsar. At that time, there remained two months and twenty-one days until Janmashtami, so the date was postponed to coincide with Janmashtami -- hence it was said that Sadguru Jivandasji departed for his divine abode on the day of Janmashtami. However, Harmaba had actually departed for her own divine abode on the fifth of the bright half of Bhadrapad. Nevertheless, we continue to observe the fifth of the bright half of Bhadrapad as the day of Maharaj Jivandasji's departure for his divine abode.

(Here the Samagam is complete.)

_Rasik jan Jivan bhaye, kini bhakti prakash. Nahana nikat bolayke, rakhya charan nivas. ||1||_ (Jivan became a rasik devotee, one absorbed in loving devotion, and revealed the light of devotion. Calling Nahana [Nana Parekh] close to him, he kept him dwelling at his feet.)

Jivandasji became a devotee absorbed in the delight of loving devotion, and he revealed loving devotion to the world. He called Nana Parekh close to him and kept him under his refuge. (Nana Parekh lived in the time of Dwarkadas.)

_Gaam hamara Darapara, sai hamara Ram. Sadguru Jivandasji, Parakh dhariya naam. ||2||_ (My village is Darapara; my Lord is Ram; my sadguru is Jivandasji. I have taken the name Parakh for myself.)

Says Nana Parekh: my home village is Darapara, and my beloved deity is Ram; my sadguru is Jivandasji. I myself have taken up the name "Parakh."

(Thus ends the complete account of his departure for the divine abode.)

On Saturday, the fourth of the bright half of Bhadrapad, Samvat 2063, corresponding to 15 September 2007, at five o'clock in the early morning, Swami Jagdish Yadunath completed writing this commentary on the Samagam. He has written it according to whatever inspiration Jivanji granted him, to the best of his ability.

The portion of the manuscript concerning this account of his departure for the divine abode had been burnt. Therefore I have written this based on whatever writing survived in the burnt portion. For this account of his departure, Nana Parekh and others wrote in their own language. I have relied on Manuscript No. 79, pages 1 to 5, as well as Manuscript No. 98, pages 32 to 40, and the original Samagam text.
